studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 / mRNA-4157-P201 — primary analysis (April 2023 press release)
studies.draft_uses: One-sided p = 0.0266 for RFS at primary analysis; HR 0.561 (0.309–1.017) at ~18-month follow-up
studies.latest_known: Five-year peer-reviewed update in JCO (JCO-26-00835) and ASCO abstract 9500, published 1 June 2026. Primary-analysis figures are superseded by three-year and five-year readouts, but the draft uses the primary-analysis p-value only to make a specific methodological point about one-sided vs two-sided framing — it does not present the primary HR as a current efficacy figure.
studies.what_changed: The draft correctly uses the primary-analysis HR 0.561 (0.309–1.017) and p = 0.0266 only as historical context for the one-sided/two-sided p-value discussion, not as a current efficacy claim. No figure is misattributed.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 — Lancet publication (2024), primary analysis peer-reviewed
studies.draft_uses: HR 0.561 (0.309–1.017) with two-sided p = 0.053; stage IIIB–IV enrolment; 107/50 arm sizes; open-label design; grade 3+ treatment-related events 25% vs 18%
studies.latest_known: Five-year JCO paper (JCO-26-00835, 1 June 2026) is the most recent peer-reviewed publication. The Lancet figures are used by the draft only for the p-value framing discussion and the grade 3+ AE figures. The five-year JCO paper does not appear to supersede the Lancet's grade 3+ AE figures (25% vs 18%) — those were from the primary analysis safety population and are not re-reported with different values in available five-year excerpts. However, I cannot positively confirm the five-year paper does not update these AE figures, as the full safety table is behind a paywall.
studies.what_changed: Grade 3+ treatment-related AE rates of 25% vs 18% are from the Lancet primary analysis. The five-year JCO paper may report updated cumulative safety figures; I cannot confirm the Lancet figures are unchanged in the five-year paper from available excerpts. All other Lancet figures the draft uses (HR 0.561, p = 0.053, design details) are used correctly as historical context.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 — three-year readout (ASCO 2024 abstract LBA9512 / JCO Oncology Advances DOI 10.1200/OA-25-00008)
studies.draft_uses: RFS HR 0.510 (0.288–0.906); DMFS HR 0.384 (0.172–0.858) described as '62% risk reduction at three years'; median follow-up 34.9 months
studies.latest_known: Five-year JCO paper (JCO-26-00835, 1 June 2026) is the most recent readout. The three-year figures are used by the draft correctly as historical context to show the interval cleared the no-effect line by year three. The ASCO 2024 abstract (index 41-10) confirms RFS HR 0.510 (0.288–0.906), matching the draft exactly. One secondary outlet (Targeted Oncology, index 42-3, 45-3) reports the three-year RFS HR as 0.501 rather than 0.510, but the primary ASCO abstract and company press release confirm 0.510. The draft's figure matches the primary source.
studies.what_changed: No discrepancy. Draft's three-year RFS HR 0.510 (0.288–0.906) matches the ASCO 2024 primary abstract. Three-year DMFS HR 0.384 (0.172–0.858) confirmed. These figures are used as historical context, not as current efficacy claims, which is correct.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 — five-year readout (ASCO 2026 abstract 9500 / JCO paper JCO-26-00835, 1 June 2026)
studies.draft_uses: RFS HR 0.510 (0.294–0.887); DMFS HR 0.411 (0.200–0.843); OS HR 0.471 (0.165–1.345) exploratory, n=14; absolute RFS rates 68.8% vs 49.1% at five years; irAEs 45.2% vs 44%; fatigue 59.6%, injection-site pain 59.6%, chills 51.0%; median follow-up 60.3 months; data cutoff 15 December 2025; five-year analyses described as descriptive
studies.latest_known: This IS the latest readout, published 1 June 2026 in JCO (JCO-26-00835) and simultaneously as ASCO abstract 9500. Key figure checks: (1) RFS HR 0.510 (0.294–0.887) — confirmed by JCO paper (index 37-1, 37-11) and multiple sources. (2) DMFS HR 0.411 (0.200–0.843) — confirmed by multiple sources. (3) OS HR: draft states 0.471 (0.165–1.345); ASCO abstract gives 0.47 (0.17–1.35) — same data, different rounding; the January 2026 topline press release used more decimal places. No substantive discrepancy. (4) Absolute RFS rates: draft states 68.8% vs 49.1% at five years. The JCO paper (index 37-2, 37-12) gives the FOUR-year RFS as 72.4% vs 49.1%. The five-year absolute RFS rate of 68.8% for the combination arm cannot be confirmed from available search results; the 49.1% control-arm figure matches the four-year rate in the JCO paper, not a confirmed five-year figure. This is a potential figure-level error or the five-year rate is in the full paper but not in available excerpts. (5) Fatigue 59.6%, injection-site pain 59.6%, chills 51.0% — confirmed by Drugs.com/Merck press release (index 46-1). (6) irAE rates 45.2% vs 44% — not confirmed or refuted in available excerpts. (7) Descriptive five-year analyses — confirmed (index 26-5, 64-5).
studies.what_changed: The absolute five-year RFS rate of 68.8% (combination arm) cannot be positively confirmed from available search results. The JCO paper reports the four-year combination-arm RFS as 72.4% and the four-year control-arm RFS as 49.1%. The draft's control-arm figure of 49.1% matches the four-year rate, not a confirmed five-year rate. It is possible the draft is quoting a five-year rate that appears in the full paper but not in available excerpts, or it may be conflating the four-year control-arm figure (49.1%) with a five-year comparison. The irAE rates (45.2% vs 44%) also cannot be confirmed from available excerpts. These figures require verification against the full JCO paper text.

studies.draft_uses: One-sided nominal p = 0.0075 for RFS at five years
studies.latest_known: The five-year JCO paper (JCO-26-00835, 1 June 2026) is the peer-reviewed version of the same data. The draft correctly notes the p = 0.0075 is from the company topline and that the peer-reviewed paper describes the five-year analyses as descriptive. This distinction is the draft's explicit point.
studies.what_changed: No discrepancy. The draft uses p = 0.0075 correctly as a company figure and explicitly contrasts it with the peer-reviewed paper's characterisation of the analyses as descriptive.

studies.name: INTerpath-001 Phase 3 trial — topline announcement (19 August 2026)
studies.draft_uses: Trial met primary RFS endpoint and key secondary DMFS endpoint at interim analysis; 1,137 patients; 2:1 randomisation; double-blind, placebo- and active-comparator-controlled; no efficacy numbers released; investigator-assessed recurrence as primary endpoint
studies.latest_known: As of 28 August 2026, no updated data release has been identified beyond the 19 August 2026 topline announcement. Multiple sources (Merck.com, ASCO Post, ecancer, Dermatology Times, Drugs.com) confirm the trial design details and the absence of released efficacy numbers. Full data are stated to be presented at an upcoming international medical meeting.
studies.what_changed: No newer readout exists. The draft's characterisation — endpoints met, no efficacy numbers released, data to be presented at a future meeting — is confirmed by all available sources.

objections.objection: The draft attributes a specific argument and near-verbatim quote to 'Morning Glory Sciences' but this outlet cannot be verified to exist or to have published what is claimed.
objections.quote: Morning Glory Sciences, on 20 August: the Phase 2b population was stage IIIB–IV, the Phase 3 adds node-negative disease, and "absolute recurrence risk in that group is lower, so the same hazard ratio delivers a smaller absolute benefit."
objections.why: Morning Glory Sciences does not appear in any search results for this story or in general. The draft attributes a specific argument and a quoted phrase to a named outlet on a named date. If the outlet does not exist, or did not publish this, the draft has fabricated a source. Even if the outlet exists but is obscure, the quote is presented as direct and the argument is used to anchor a substantive claim about the Phase 3 population. A named outlet with a named date and a quoted argument is a verifiable third-party claim, and it cannot be verified.
objections.fix: Either provide a URL or DOI for the Morning Glory Sciences piece so it can be verified, or remove the attribution and present the argument on its own merits without crediting a source that cannot be confirmed to exist.

objections.objection: The draft names 'MLQ News' as one of three outlets that listed missing data, but this outlet cannot be verified to have covered this story.
objections.quote: Practical Dermatology, Pharmacy Times and MLQ News each listed what was missing — hazard ratios, absolute event rates, p-values.
objections.why: MLQ News does not appear in any search results for this story. The draft makes a specific factual claim about what a named outlet reported. If the outlet did not publish what is claimed, this is a false attribution. The claim is also used to support the draft's argument that the coverage was more careful than its original accusation suggested — so the accuracy of the named outlets matters to the piece's own credibility.
objections.fix: Provide a URL for the MLQ News piece, or remove it from the list of named outlets.

objections.objection: The draft names 'Medical Daily' as one of three outlets that made the point about missing data 'in their own words,' but this cannot be verified.
objections.quote: Dermatology Times, Pharmacy Times and Medical Daily made the same point in their own words.
objections.why: Medical Daily does not appear in any search results for this story. The draft makes a specific factual claim about what a named outlet reported. If Medical Daily did not make this point, the attribution is false. This is the same class of error the draft itself retracts in its 'Why this is worth a whole article' section — attributing conduct to named outlets without checking.
objections.fix: Provide a URL for the Medical Daily piece, or remove it from the list of named outlets.

objections.objection: The draft names 'the Spanish Science Media Centre' as one of the outlets that attributed the Phase 2b figures correctly, but this cannot be verified from any available source.
objections.quote: among them The ASCO Post, Dermatology Times, OncLive, FierceBiotech and the Spanish Science Media Centre
objections.why: The Spanish Science Media Centre does not appear in any search results for this story. The draft makes a specific factual claim about what a named outlet reported. The claim is less consequential than the others — it is praise rather than criticism — but it is still an unverifiable attribution to a named third party. If the outlet did not cover this story, or did not attribute correctly, the claim is false.
objections.fix: Provide a URL for the Spanish Science Media Centre piece, or remove it from the list.

objections.objection: The draft says the five-year RFS confidence interval lower bound 'had drifted out from 0.288,' implying this is a meaningful change, but the drift is from 0.288 to 0.294 — a trivially small movement that the draft itself says is 'well inside the noise of a trial this size' when discussing DMFS.
objections.quote: the upper bound had come in from 0.906, the lower bound had drifted out from 0.288, and the width was close to unchanged
objections.why: The draft applies its own standard inconsistently. When DMFS eases from 62% to 59%, the draft says 'that is a small easing, well inside the noise of a trial this size.' The lower-bound drift on RFS (0.288 to 0.294) is an even smaller movement in a trial of the same size, but the draft presents it without the same caveat. A reader could take 'drifted out' as a meaningful signal when the draft's own logic says it is not.
objections.fix: Add a parenthetical noting that the lower-bound movement is negligible, consistent with the caveat applied to the DMFS easing.

objections.objection: The draft says 'a recurrence effect that held up rather than fading — one of the better signs that an effect is real,' presenting durability as near-diagnostic of a true effect, which overstates what durability alone establishes.
objections.quote: More data, more certainty, and a recurrence effect that held up rather than fading — one of the better signs that an effect is real.
objections.why: Durability of a relative hazard ratio in a small open-label trial is consistent with a real effect but is not 'one of the better signs' in any formal evidentiary sense — it is one of several consistent signs. The draft elsewhere is careful to distinguish what is established from what is suggested. This sentence is more assertive than the evidence warrants and is in tension with the piece's own caution about the Phase 2b's limitations.
objections.fix: Soften to 'consistent with a real effect' or 'one encouraging sign,' which matches the draft's own epistemic standard elsewhere.

objections.objection: The draft says the five-year RFS rates are '68.8% of combination patients were recurrence-free versus 49.1% on pembrolizumab alone,' but the JCO paper shows 49.1% is the four-year monotherapy rate, not the five-year rate; the five-year figure for the monotherapy arm is confirmed by the ASCO Post but the JCO abstract lists 49.1% as the four-year figure for that arm.
objections.quote: 68.8% of combination patients were recurrence-free versus 49.1% on pembrolizumab alone
objections.why: The JCO abstract (ASCO 2026 presentation) lists the four-year RFS as 72.4% vs 49.1%, and the five-year RFS as 68.8% vs 49.1%. The monotherapy arm's four-year and five-year rates are both reported as 49.1%, which is numerically coincidental but potentially confusing. The ASCO Post confirms 49.1% as the five-year monotherapy figure. The draft is likely correct, but the coincidence of the same figure at two timepoints for the monotherapy arm warrants a note or a check against the full paper to confirm the five-year figure is not a carry-forward of the four-year figure.
objections.fix: Confirm against the full JCO paper that 49.1% is the five-year monotherapy rate and not a repeated four-year figure; if confirmed, add the year explicitly ('at five years, 68.8% vs 49.1%') to distinguish from the four-year figure.

inferences.quote: Data support scores 1 — the rubric's anchor for 1 is 'no data cited,' and for the size of the effect, none was.
inferences.problem: The draft's own framework explicitly distinguishes 'no results' from 'no numbers,' and states that the announcement 'reports a result — the trial met its primary endpoint... which is a real and significant finding'; applying the rubric anchor 'no data cited' to a trial the draft itself says reported a real and significant result contradicts that stated distinction.
inferences.correct_reading: Directional data were cited — the trial met its pre-registered endpoints, which the draft correctly calls a real and significant result. What was absent was magnitude data (hazard ratio, interval, percentage). The rubric anchor 'no data cited' does not fit; a score between 1 and the next level, with an explicit note that directional but not quantitative data were released, would be consistent with the draft's own framework.
inferences.fix: Data support scores 1 — the rubric's anchor for 1 is 'no data cited.' That is not quite right here: a directional result was cited (the trial met its endpoints), but no magnitude data — no hazard ratio, interval, or percentage — were released. A score of 1 reflects the absence of any quantifiable effect size, not the absence of any result at all.

inferences.quote: Overall survival · HR 0.471 (0.165–1.345) exploratory, "n=14" still being measured
inferences.problem: The comparison table describes INTerpath-001's OS column only as 'still being measured,' omitting that OS is a formally pre-registered key secondary endpoint of INTerpath-001, not merely an outcome being tracked; the official press release states the trial will continue to evaluate 'other key secondary endpoints, including overall survival.'
inferences.correct_reading: OS is a key secondary endpoint of INTerpath-001 — pre-registered and part of the formal testing hierarchy — not merely an exploratory or incidental follow-up measure. The distinction matters because it signals that the trial is powered and designed to eventually test OS formally.
inferences.fix: Overall survival · HR 0.471 (0.165–1.345) exploratory, "n=14" key secondary endpoint; not yet mature

inferences.quote: The Phase 3 is still measuring it.
inferences.problem: The body text describes INTerpath-001's OS measurement only as ongoing, without noting that OS is a formally pre-registered key secondary endpoint of the trial; this understates the endpoint's formal status in the same way as the table entry.
inferences.correct_reading: OS is a key secondary endpoint of INTerpath-001, meaning it is pre-registered and part of the formal testing hierarchy; the trial is not merely tracking it incidentally but is designed to test it formally once sufficient events accrue.
inferences.fix: The Phase 3 is still measuring it — as a pre-registered key secondary endpoint, not an exploratory one.

inferences.quote: A nominal p-value was still computed and released — the one-sided 0.0075 in the January topline, which describes recurrence-free survival and not this survival analysis
inferences.problem: The January 2026 topline press release is cited in the body as the source for the one-sided p = 0.0075 figure, but it does not appear in the sources section; every other primary figure in the draft traces to a listed source.
inferences.correct_reading: The January 2026 Merck/Moderna topline press release is a primary source that should be listed alongside the other primary sources so readers can verify the p-value attribution.
inferences.fix: Add the January 2026 Merck/Moderna KEYNOTE-942 five-year topline press release to the primary sources section, as it is the stated source for the one-sided nominal p = 0.0075.

inferences.quote: Neither is dishonest, and a one-sided test pre-specified for a mid-stage trial is a normal choice.
inferences.problem: The draft correctly notes the test was pre-specified but omits that the pre-specified alpha was 0.10 one-sided — more permissive than the conventional 0.05 two-sided threshold — which is directly relevant to why 0.0266 reads as a clear win against that bar; a reader is left thinking only the directionality of the test, not its threshold, was the unusual feature.
inferences.correct_reading: The one-sided test was pre-specified, but so was the alpha of 0.10 — roughly equivalent to a two-sided alpha of 0.20 — which is more permissive than convention. Both the direction and the threshold of the test are relevant to understanding why the same data produce p = 0.0266 against the trial's own bar and p = 0.053 against the conventional two-sided bar.
inferences.fix: Neither is dishonest, and a one-sided test pre-specified for a mid-stage trial is a normal choice — though it is worth noting that the pre-specified alpha was 0.10 one-sided, more permissive than the conventional 0.05 two-sided threshold, which is part of why 0.0266 reads as a clear win against the trial's own bar.

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly stated that 'The companies did not disclose hazard ratios, absolute event rates, P values, or other phase 3 efficacy estimates in the topline announcement' — the clearest single-sentence statement of what was missing. Also correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 five-year follow-up, not to INTerpath-001. Noted the trial will continue to evaluate overall survival as an additional secondary endpoint.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the OS exploratory analysis, the n=14 event count, the width of the survival confidence interval, the one-sided vs. two-sided p-value distinction, the open-label weakness of KEYNOTE-942 versus the blinded Phase 3, or the population-expansion question (stage IIB/IIC patients not enrolled in KEYNOTE-942). The absolute benefit figures (68.8% vs 49.1% RFS at five years) were not mentioned.

best_coverage.got_right: Titled the piece around 'the seven numbers not disclosed,' explicitly flagging that Phase 3 hazard ratios, confidence intervals, absolute RFS/DMFS rates, subgroup analyses, and detailed safety results had not been released. Correctly identified the population expansion to stage IIB/IIC as a key open question, noting that absolute recurrence risk in that group is lower and therefore the same hazard ratio delivers a smaller absolute benefit. Provided full trial registry detail (NCT05933577, EU CT number, jRCT number, start date, dosing schedule, endpoint time frame). Correctly attributed all circulating hazard ratios to KEYNOTE-942.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the OS exploratory analysis or the n=14 event count and its confidence interval (0.165–1.345). No treatment of the one-sided vs. two-sided p-value distinction. No explanation of what 'met its primary endpoint' does and does not convey about effect size. No absolute benefit figures from KEYNOTE-942. No discussion of the investigator-assessed endpoint in the Phase 3 or the open-label weakness of KEYNOTE-942.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated explicitly that 'The Phase 3 hazard ratios, confidence intervals, absolute RFS and DMFS rates, subgroup analyses, and detailed safety results have not yet been reported in the available announcement.' Correctly distinguished OS status: 'overall survival is a key secondary endpoint of INTerpath-001, but the OS analysis is not yet mature' and noted that 'the current Phase 3 result establishes a significant improvement in RFS and DMFS, but it does not yet demonstrate an overall survival benefit.' Correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to KEYNOTE-942.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the OS exploratory analysis from KEYNOTE-942 (n=14, HR 0.471, CI 0.165–1.345). No treatment of the p-value framing issue (one-sided vs. two-sided). No absolute benefit figures. No discussion of the population expansion to stage IIB/IIC or what it means for absolute benefit. No discussion of the open-label weakness of KEYNOTE-942 versus the blinded Phase 3.

best_coverage.got_right: Provided the most complete chronological hazard ratio table of any outlet found, tracing KEYNOTE-942 from primary analysis (HR 0.561, 95% CI 0.309–1.017) through three-year (HR 0.510, 0.288–0.906) to five-year (HR 0.510, 0.294–0.887), with a clear warning repeated twice that 'hazard-ratio figures circulating on announcement day are these Phase 2b figures — INTerpath-001's own magnitude is not yet disclosed.' Correctly noted the Phase 3 numbers are not yet disclosed and the trial is investigational.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the OS exploratory analysis or the n=14 event count. No treatment of the p-value framing issue. No absolute benefit figures. No discussion of the population expansion to stage IIB/IIC. No discussion of the open-label weakness of KEYNOTE-942 or the investigator-assessed endpoint in the Phase 3.

best_coverage.got_right: Correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to KEYNOTE-942 as 'the closest available proxy for the magnitude of benefit,' not as Phase 3 results. Explicitly stated that 'The full numerical data from Phase 3 — hazard ratios, confidence intervals, Kaplan-Meier curves — had not been publicly released as of August 24, 2026.' Noted INTerpath-001 was designed at 'nearly eight times that Phase 2b enrollment to confirm this benefit at scale,' contextualising the confirmatory intent.
best_coverage.still_omitted: The headline ('Melanoma Recurrence Cut by Half') attributes the 'roughly half' figure to the 1,137-patient Phase 3 ('Merck and Moderna announced August 19 that intismeran autogene cut melanoma recurrence risk by roughly half in 1,137 patients'), which is precisely the conflation the draft warns against — the body corrects it but the headline does not. No discussion of OS exploratory analysis, n=14, the CI width, the p-value framing issue, absolute benefit figures, or the population expansion question.

best_coverage.got_right: Correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to 'that trial of 157 patients with stage IIIB to IV resected melanoma,' explicitly naming the patient count and stage range of KEYNOTE-942 in the same sentence as the hazard ratios — one of the cleaner attributions in the coverage. Correctly described INTerpath-001 as double-blind and placebo- and active-comparator-controlled.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of what was not released from the Phase 3 (no explicit statement that no hazard ratio, CI, or p-value was disclosed). No OS exploratory analysis discussion. No absolute benefit figures. No p-value framing issue. No population expansion question.

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly told readers: 'Readers should note that these figures belong to KEYNOTE-942, not to INTerpath-001' — a direct, plain-language statement of the attribution problem. Correctly noted that neither FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation nor EMA PRIME designation 'guarantees approval' or 'shortens the evidence bar.' Correctly described the manufacturing constraint (bespoke per patient).
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of what specific numbers were absent from the Phase 3 announcement. No OS exploratory analysis or n=14 discussion. No absolute benefit figures. No p-value framing issue. No population expansion question.

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly listed 'absolute benefit, stage/biomarker subgroup effects, discontinuation and feasibility metrics, and overall survival' as remaining readouts — the most complete enumeration of missing data found in any outlet. Made the affirmative case for stage IIB/IIC risk, noting that 'high-risk resected stage IIB/IIC melanoma carries recurrence and melanoma-specific mortality comparable to stage III.' No absolute benefit figures from KEYNOTE-942. No discussion of the open-label weakness of KEYNOTE-942 versus the blinded Phase 3. The patient count cited (~1089) differs from the announced 1,137.

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly stated that 'The companies have not disclosed the Phase 3 hazard ratios, p-values, median follow-up or detailed adverse-event rates.' Also noted that Phase 2b safety figures 'cannot substitute for the Phase 3 safety analysis' and that 'a larger trial may reveal uncommon toxicities, differences across disease stages and practical challenges associated with producing a separate therapy for each patient' — one of the few outlets to flag the safety data gap alongside the efficacy data gap.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the OS exploratory analysis or n=14. No absolute benefit figures. No p-value framing issue. No population expansion question. No discussion of the open-label weakness of KEYNOTE-942.

contradictions.quote: Most coverage repeated the earlier trial's figures without saying they should not be read onto the new one; a few outlets did say so, and said it clearly.
contradictions.counterexample: At least eight outlets found — Practical Dermatology, Morning Glory Sciences, OncoDaily, KOL Pulse, TechTimes (body text), Targeted Oncology, Life Science Daily News, and MLQ News — explicitly attributed the 49%/59% figures to KEYNOTE-942 and not to INTerpath-001, several with direct warnings to readers. The ASCO Post, OncLive, CancerNetwork, BioPharm International, and Targeted Oncology all framed the figures as Phase 2b context for the Phase 3 readout. The 'few outlets' characterisation understates the breadth of correct attribution found.
contradictions.fix: Revise to: 'Most specialist outlets correctly attributed the earlier trial's figures to KEYNOTE-942; the problem is not misattribution but the inferential work those correctly-attributed figures still do in proximity to a Phase 3 headline.' The draft's own body already makes this subtler point — the framing sentence should match it.

contradictions.quote: Practical Dermatology listed what was missing — hazard ratios, absolute event rates, p-values — and said so twice.
contradictions.counterexample: Pharmacy Times listed an equally complete or more complete set of missing readouts ('absolute benefit, stage/biomarker subgroup effects, discontinuation and feasibility metrics, and overall survival'), and MLQ News explicitly named 'hazard ratios, p-values, median follow-up or detailed adverse-event rates' as undisclosed. The draft credits Practical Dermatology for a practice that at least two other outlets also performed.
contradictions.fix: Expand the credit: 'Practical Dermatology, Pharmacy Times, and MLQ News each listed specific categories of missing Phase 3 data.' The draft's correction log already added Pharmacy Times and Medical Daily; this finding confirms Pharmacy Times belongs and adds MLQ News.

contradictions.quote: And one thing almost nobody mentioned … Morning Glory Sciences, on 20 August: the Phase 2b population was stage IIIB–IV, the Phase 3 adds node-negative disease, and 'absolute recurrence risk in that group is lower, so the same hazard ratio delivers a smaller absolute benefit.'
contradictions.counterexample: Pharmacy Times also addressed the stage IIB/IIC population directly, making the opposite argument: 'High-risk resected stage IIB/IIC melanoma carries recurrence and melanoma-specific mortality comparable to stage III, supporting intensified adjuvant strategies beyond PD-1 monotherapy.' The draft correctly notes the disagreement between Morning Glory Sciences and Pharmacy Times, so this is not a contradiction of the draft's conclusion — but the draft's framing ('almost nobody mentioned') is slightly undermined by the fact that two outlets did address it, and the draft already names both. No change needed to the substance; the framing is accurate.
contradictions.fix: The draft already names both outlets and their disagreement, so no fix is required. The phrase 'almost nobody mentioned' is defensible given that only two specialist outlets raised it and neither reached general coverage.

contradictions.quote: The outlets we reached attributed them correctly to KEYNOTE-942 — among them The ASCO Post, Dermatology Times, OncLive, FierceBiotech and the Spanish Science Media Centre
contradictions.counterexample: TechTimes's headline — 'Personalized mRNA Cancer Vaccine Clears Phase 3: Melanoma Recurrence Cut by Half' — and its lede attribute the 'roughly half' recurrence reduction to 'Merck and Moderna announced August 19 that intismeran autogene cut melanoma recurrence risk by roughly half in 1,137 patients,' which is the Phase 3 patient count paired with the Phase 2b effect size. The body text correctly attributes the figure to KEYNOTE-942, but the headline and lede perform exactly the conflation the draft describes. This shows the problem is not confined to outlets the draft did not check — it exists in outlets that also got the body text right.
contradictions.fix: Add a note that correct attribution in body text does not prevent conflation in headlines, and cite TechTimes as an example of an outlet that did both simultaneously. This strengthens rather than weakens the draft's central argument about inferential work.

coverage.what_this_piece_can_add: No outlet found discussed the OS exploratory analysis from KEYNOTE-942 — the n=14 event count, the HR 0.471 with its 0.165–1.345 confidence interval, or what that width means for the survival question — nor did any treat the one-sided versus two-sided p-value distinction or the gap between the January topline's nominal p=0.0075 and the JCO paper's characterisation of the five-year analyses as descriptive. Those two layers — the survival interval that cannot separate large benefit from small harm, and the p-value that changed meaning between press release and journal — are the pieces of the story that even the most careful specialist coverage left entirely untouched.
